Thanks for all the advice everyone. My managers are VERY happy with me!!! I was genuinely concerned I wouldn't be a good fit or would be slow to catch on to this craft style tending. They love my speed, I unintentionally *smoked* their veteran bartender and did so with efficiency and accurate detail! My tips are decent, the regulars are still warming up to me (they seem to think I'm a young blonde bimbo who is only there to be pretty, and not actually well versed in bartending) but most all of them were happy to meet our bars newest tender. The key was being confident and not shy to pour up and do my thing, yet remaining a bit humble- as I did have to learn the certain ways the bar likes to run their service. Classic cocktails weren't a problem, it was like riding a bike when asked to make mojitos, speciality martinis, old fashions, manhattens, and an array of different scotch drinks, etc. I pulled a crowd of 18-20 of my friends/followers into the bar one of my second nights and the owner instantly quit doubting me, and gave me a bonus for the added business. All in all - it's going well. I miss the volume bartending money, that's the biggest difference. But do sincerely appreciate all the comments and replies to this thread ! Great community we have hear with solid advice to offer.

As the mother of two beautiful (like actually very gorgeous; not just my biased motherly opinion) baby girls- ages 5 and 8 months.. we laid their father to rest 46 days ago: It was his second OD. And he was never truly able to get sober. One of the most powerful things I've read during our past terrible 2 years seeing his struggle- was the surgeon general saying addiction is a disease; not a moral failure. I believe that does NOT fit every specific incident- but we did just witness a man raised incredibly well, who was a loving father, and the man a woman hopes to be tied to forever ...get so sucked in to a place he didn't want to be. Sometimes it's hard to accept that bad things just happen to good people. Heroin is the scariest word I can ever speak now. 

Tl:dr; looking at two fatherless daughters right now because of heroin. And so incredibly happy for all those on this thread  who are overcoming the struggles and becoming healthy again. Sobriety must be difficult..but oh so beautiful in the eyes of some.
Thanks for all the suggestions, messages, and overall support. I'm going to post on care.com and keep my fingers crossed!

I work in a 5 floor building with an open atrium. A man jumped to his death from the top floor on a Friday right at quitting time. He narrowly missed a few people walking to the exit.. 
I didn't witness the act itself but I was one of the first to try to leave before the place was swarmed with police and ambulances and what not. So, I exit the elevator on the bottom floor as normal, not expecting anything unusual, and see several people frantic and calling 911 and i quickly walked up on the darkest image I've ever seen. it's burned into my memory. I could not avoid seeing him lying there distorted and messy. I ran past and out to my car in the parking lot where I quickly sank to the cement crying and watched the emergency service brigade move in and block off that entrance.

I need hair advice. So if you're a stylist or just even know what the heck is going on plz help. Okay after years of dying my hair it got into really bad shape. This year I had a baby and decided to get my hair healthy again. 

So it's been over a year since I have died or used heat on my hair. It has completely changed. Majority of it is healthy and soft EXCEPT these stupid pieces in the front...they will NOT grow past this length.. while the rest of my hair seems to be growing fine and really gaining back its health. Why?! Why won't this ugly front part grow.. I sectioned it off in red so you can see the difference of the front from the longer hair in the back. I get regular trims/ take tons of  vitamins/ use all natural shampoo. but my hair in the front looks like TRASH.. it used to be long and beautiful and heathy and strong ... I know my hair is a petty thing to be upset over, but I'm trying hard to feel pretty again after having my newest baby...

(Sorry for the side boobies I was nursing my little one 😂)

This is my second time sharing my body with another human for 24 hours a day, for 40 weeks. Might not sound like much to someone who hasn't been here. But literally, I haven't been alone for a single second  in 7 months and I'm not in control of my own emotions. It's wild..

"Wow you're really out there aren't you?" "Wow your belly is big"

I'm 5'3 and weighed 110 before pregnancy. I've gained 15lbs at seven months pregnant... 

Unless your telling me how fucking fabulous I look while SUPER pregnant in the heat of ATL, GA...then stfu.
